rv.q: Other dualities—between distance and intimacy, life and death, art and commerce—pervade Smith’s quietly shattering piece of remembrance and reclamation.

Roger Guenveur Smith’s homage to his late friend is moving and evocative, delivered in a singular style that streams snippets of nonstop memories into a revealing retrospective of their times, their time together, and their impact on one another and the world.
Smith’s deliverance itself is striking and haunting.
The substance of the show proves less important than its style, with Smith proving mesmerizing in his smooth, beat poetry-style delivery of the elliptical text.
Doing so, he memorializes his late friend honorably.

Roger Guenveur Smith delivers a captivating celebration of community in his solo show, honoring not just Jean-Michel Basquiat but the sprawling collection of people who are inextricably embedded into their bond and their works.
That turns out to be all Smith needs to mesmerize us for 60 minutes.
It doesn't, but what's more confounding is, it doesn't tell us much about Basquiat.
In Honor of Jean-Michel Basquiat engulfed and overwhelmed me in its sincerity, its poetry, and its outcry.
This is downtown theater at its best.
In Honor of Jean-Michel Basquiat is fascinating, discursive, poetic — and delivered in about an hour with the barefoot confidence of a veteran sideman from some smoky downtown club.

cn.t: Roger Guenveur Smith's personal tribute to Basquiat earns strong reviews for its poetic, jazz-inflected storytelling and vivid performance, though some find the impressionistic collage structure occasionally unfocused.
